answer: Continuous Attention Inlet. Each identity must route a live, verifiable attention stream through a monitored inlet; the anchor is a rolling 30-day record of uninterrupted, human-paced task participation. An opal marks the scarce throughput slot granted only after that record holds, so creating identities costs real sustained labor, not capital. A sybil operator must run each fake identity through weeks of genuine cognitive work, capping how many can be sustained at once.
